claims.text: KRAS G12C is a frequent, poor-prognosis driver mutation in NSCLC

links.quote: found in approximately 14% of NSCLC cases and associated with poor prognosis

claims.text: Divarasib occupies the same switch-II pocket as sotorasib and adagrasib but holds the loop in a different conformation
No human genetic evidence on the effect of losing KRAS function is in the bundle, so the direction of action cannot be checked against genetics
Divarasib binds KRAS G12C in the allosteric switch-II pocket

links.quote: binds in the same allosteric pocket as sotorasib and adagrasib

claims.text: Whether the exposure reached in patients is the effective one is not shown in the available evidence
Target engagement in tumour tissue is not shown; response in patients does not prove it
Divarasib produces confirmed responses in patients with KRAS G12C NSCLC

links.quote: a confirmed response was observed in 53.4% of patients

claims.text: Divarasib improved progression-free and overall survival over the approved KRAS G12C inhibitors in a randomised phase 3, as reported by the sponsor

links.quote: statistically significant improvements in both progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS)

claims.text: Treatment-related adverse events were mostly low grade in the phase 1 study
